import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 250

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/250](https://www.erdosproblems.com/250)
-/

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos250

/--
Is
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\sigma(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? Here $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of divisors function.

The answer is yes, as shown by Nesterenko [Ne96].

[Ne96] Nesterenko, Yu V., _Modular functions and transcendence questions_,
Mat. Sb. 187 *9* (1996), 1319--1348.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_250  : (∀ x, HasSum (fun (n : ℕ) => σ 1 n / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) x → Irrational x) ↔
    answer(True):= by
  sorry

end Erdos250

findings.description: The docstring’s [Ne96] reference combines the original journal abbreviation `Mat. Sb.` with the English translation’s pagination, `1319--1348`. This is only a bibliographic slip; the cited work does establish the affirmative answer and the Lean statement is mathematically faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Nesterenko’s paper, first-page header, distinguishes “Sbornik: Mathematics 187:9 1319–1348” from “Matematicheskii Sbornik 187:9 65–96”. MathNet likewise gives the English citation as “Sb. Math., 187:9 (1996), 1319–1348”: https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/sm158 and https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sm&paperid=158&what=fullteng&option_lang=eng.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `Mat. Sb.` to `Sb. Math.` while retaining pages 1319–1348, or retain the original journal name and use pages 65–96.

reformulations.difference: Instead of directly asserting irrationality of the series indexed by positive integers, Lean says that every real number satisfying `HasSum` for the zero-indexed series is irrational, and places `answer(True)` on the right of the equivalence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib’s `σ 1 n` is exactly the sum of positive divisors of n, with `σ 1 0 = 0`, so the added zeroth summand contributes nothing. The bound `σ 1 n ≤ n²` gives absolute convergence by comparison with ∑ n²/2ⁿ. Consequently the HasSum hypothesis is satisfiable, unconditional summation agrees with ordinary partial-sum convergence, and uniqueness of the real sum makes the universally quantified implication equivalent to irrationality of that sum. Finally, `P ↔ answer(True)` is equivalent to P. The complete equivalence with `Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (σ 1 (n + 1) : ℝ) / 2^(n + 1))` was proved independently in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` as `Review250.full_statement_equivalence`.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. The source records an affirmative solution, agreeing with `research solved` and `answer(True)`. Nesterenko’s Corollary 2 makes P(1/2) transcendental; since P(1/2) = 1 − 24∑σ(n)/2ⁿ, it supports the stated irrationality result. Scratch checks verified the real-valued division, the zero/one/two boundary cases, small sigma values, and convergence. The final scratch file compiles without errors or warnings, and its equivalence proof has no sorryAx dependency. The reviewed file was not modified.
